summary: For D8/D13, I derived three design constraints, each labeled design inference, mapping Dung's extension semantics to contradiction handling and belief revision in the many-to-many Q/A graph. The only dossier content I can cite is the single workspace file, papers/text/dung-1995-argumentation.txt, which provides the definitions (preferred, grounded, stable extensions; admissible/acceptable; characteristic function; semantic coincidence conditions). I explicitly separate the observed definitions from my design inferences. Counterevidence I noticed: (a) the source does not mention belief revision or answer graphs, so any such mapping is inference; (b) the source warns that stable extensions may not exist and that preferred extensions may not be unique, so the design must treat these as failure/variability modes; (c) the source warns that general extension computation is incomputable (page 25), so the design must bound the argument set to stay tractable. Sufficiency is partial because I only have the Dung file in hand and cannot support the broader synthesis, but for this node's design-inference deliverable the source is adequate.
unresolved: I cannot cite any of the other six corpus files because their contents were not provided in this dossier; the design must therefore rely only on Dung's formalism for contradiction/revision.

The exact trigger semantics for when a revision is performed (e.g., new answer posted, conflict edge added, explicit user request) is not defined in this node; it is left to the runtime specification.

The treatment of weighted or typed conflicts (e.g., specificity vs. contradiction) is not addressed by Dung's binary attack relation; the source only mentions two kinds of attacks but not a formalization.
